package_info.package_name: Agent Tesla (delivered via crafted Excel document and dasHost.exe)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware delivered via phishing and Windows executable)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects all delivered samples in this campaign)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a multi-stage malware campaign that uses a crafted Excel document exploiting CVE-2017-11882/CVE-2018-0802 to deliver and execute Agent Tesla, a .NET-based RAT and data stealer. The malware achieves persistence, steals credentials, keylogs, takes screenshots, and exfiltrates data via SMTP, exhibiting clear malicious intent and behavior.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Crafted equation data exploiting CVE-2017-11882/CVE-2018-0802 to execute shellcode via EQNEDT32.EXE.
malicious_snippets.code_language: shellcode (x86, embedded in OLE equation data)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the Excel document is opened, the crafted equation data triggers a memory corruption in EQNEDT32.EXE, causing it to execute embedded shellcode that downloads and executes a remote payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exploiting a known RCE vulnerability in Office to execute arbitrary code is a hallmark of malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Excel documents should not contain equation data that triggers code execution or exploits vulnerabilities.
key_indicators: Presence of shellcode in OLE equation data
Automatic code execution on document open

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Shellcode calls URLDownloadToFileW() to download hxxp://23[.]95.128.195/3355/chromium.exe and saves as %TEMP%/dasHost.exe; then calls ShellExecuteW() to run it.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After exploitation, the shellcode downloads a remote executable (Agent Tesla loader) and executes it on the victim's system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing remote binaries is a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Office documents should not download and execute arbitrary executables.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Loader extracts two modules from .NET Resources: Loader module (Cassa) and Agent Tesla payload (NyZELH bX). Uses Bitmap.GetPixel() and Color.FromArgb() to read, then decrypts and decompresses payload, loads via AppDomain.CurrentDomain.Load(), and invokes EntryPoint.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the loader stealthily extracts, decrypts, and loads the Agent Tesla payload from disguised resources, then executes it in memory.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated resource extraction, decryption, and in-memory execution are common anti-analysis and evasion techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not hide executables in disguised resources or load them dynamically in this manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software uses resource encryption for DRM, but not for self-extracting and executing hidden payloads.
key_indicators: Bitmap API misuse for payload extraction

execution_context.file_location: Agent Tesla payload module (in memory, loaded by loader)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Performs process hollowing: uses CreateProcess() to create suspended dasHost.exe, VirtualAllocEx() to allocate memory, WriteProcessMemory() to inject core module, SetThreadContext() and ResumeThread() to execute injected code.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the payload creates a new process, injects the core Agent Tesla module into it, and resumes execution, hiding the malicious code within a legitimate process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process hollowing is a well-known malware technique for evasion and persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications do not inject code into other processes in this manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, advanced debuggers or security tools may use similar techniques.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Executes: schtasks.exe /Create /TN "Updates\kCqKCO" /XML "C:\Users\Bobs\AppData\Local\Temp\tmp68E9.tmp" (task runs C:\Users\Bobs\AppData\Roaming\kCqKCO.exe at logon)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After infection, the malware creates a scheduled task to ensure persistence by running a copy of itself at user logon.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Creating hidden scheduled tasks for persistence is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers may create tasks, but not for hidden, self-replicating executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters use scheduled tasks, but with transparent user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After infection, the malware ensures persistence by adding itself to the Windows auto-run registry keys.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly uses registry auto-run for persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not silently add itself to auto-run without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software uses auto-run, but typically with user awareness.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Steals credentials from browsers, email clients, FTP clients, VPNs, and messaging apps by reading their storage locations and extracting saved passwords.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware enumerates installed software, accesses credential storage, and extracts saved credentials for exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating credentials from multiple applications is a hallmark of info-stealers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or export credentials from unrelated applications.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Calls SetWindowsHookEx() to install a keyboard hook; logs keystrokes, window titles, and timestamps to %Temp%/log.tmp; timer checks log.tmp every 20 minutes and submits via SMTP.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware records all keystrokes and periodically exfiltrates the log file via email.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Keylogging is a classic malicious surveillance technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not install global keyboard hooks or exfiltrate keystroke logs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Parental control or accessibility tools may use hooks, but not for exfiltration.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Uses GetLastInputInfo() to check user activity; if active, captures screenshot using Bitmap and Graphics APIs, saves as JPEG in memory, attaches to email for exfiltration.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware periodically captures screenshots and exfiltrates them as email attachments.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Stealthy screenshot capture and exfiltration is a common surveillance tactic in RATs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not capture and exfiltrate screenshots without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools may capture screens, but with user awareness.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Uses hardcoded SMTP server (mail.daymon.cc:587) to send emails with stolen credentials, keylogs, and screenshots as attachments. Email subjects: 'PW_{User/Computer}', 'KL_{User/Computer}', 'SC_{User/Computer}'.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware exfiltrates all collected data via email to an attacker-controlled SMTP server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating sensitive data to an external SMTP server is a clear sign of data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not send user data to unknown external servers.
key_indicators: Automated email exfiltration of sensitive data

attack_chain.action: User opens phishing email and attached Excel document.
Crafted equation data exploits CVE-2017-11882/CVE-2018-0802 to execute shellcode.
Shellcode downloads and executes Agent Tesla loader (dasHost.exe) from remote server.
Loader extracts, decrypts, and loads Agent Tesla payload from disguised resources.
Payload performs process hollowing to inject core Agent Tesla module into a new process.
Malware establishes persistence via scheduled task and registry auto-run.
Core module steals credentials, keylogs, and captures screenshots.
Exfiltrates stolen data via SMTP to attacker-controlled server.

behavioral_signatures: Office document exploiting CVE-2017-11882/CVE-2018-0802 on open
Shellcode downloading and executing remote binaries
Obfuscated .NET resource extraction and in-memory execution
Process hollowing of legitimate Windows executables
Creation of hidden scheduled tasks and registry auto-run entries
Automated exfiltration via SMTP to hardcoded servers
file_indicators: Excel OLE documents with equation data in \x01Ole10NativE streams
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents exploiting CVE-2017-11882/CVE-2018-0802, especially those with OLE equation data. Detect suspicious child processes spawned by EQNEDT32.EXE, especially those that download and execute remote binaries. Look for .NET executables with obfuscated resources and in-memory assembly loading. Alert on process hollowing behaviors (CreateProcess in suspended state, WriteProcessMemory, SetThreadContext). Monitor for creation of scheduled tasks and registry auto-run entries pointing to unknown executables in user AppData. Detect credential access from unrelated applications, keylogging hooks, and periodic screenshot capture. Flag outbound SMTP traffic to suspicious or hardcoded servers, especially with attachments or credential data.
